text:
lena: FYI a user reported that links to /guides/streaming#response-format jump to the warning box instead of the section. here's the report: https://docs.redwood.ai/guides/streaming#response-format marco: nice catch. do you have the page source? raw HTML around headings often causes docusaurus/mkdocs slug mismatch. lena: here's the relevant part copied from the page: ```md > Note: streams are newline-delimited JSON
### Response format Examples and a tiny code sample with inline <br/>.
### Examples ... ``` priya: that
wrapper is the culprit. the HTML generates a separate id and the slugifier ends up creating two similar ids. easiest fixes: replace with mkdocs admonition syntax or add an explicit heading id. marco: agree. small PR idea: convert the HTML to `!!! warning \"Note\"`, add `{#response-format}` to the heading, and remove the inline from code blocks. also add a linkcheck tweak to CI to surface duplicate slugs. lena: can you open the PR? i'll review. priya: opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3507 Patch includes: ```diff -
-### Response format -Some details with inline <br/>. -
+!!! warning \"Note\" + +### Response format {#response-format} +Some details with fenced `
` examples. ``` ci-bot: Running docs linkcheck for PR #3507 (`yarn docs:linkcheck`, `mkdocs build --strict`). docs-bot: Requested reviewers: @lena, @marco. ci-bot: Linkcheck finished: no broken anchors found. Added grep duplicate-slug check, no duplicates detected. marco: LGTM, merged. commit 9b3d4ff. lena: thanks all. i'll add a short note in the docs migration guide: \"avoid raw HTML around headings/admonitions; prefer native admonitions or explicit heading ids\" to help future contributors. priya: filing a follow-up task to run a repo-wide scan for raw HTML admonitions and missing explicit ids. putting it in the docs backlog.
